Subject: Pricing ops sync: package alignment & channel-margin evidence

Hi Lena — thanks again for the time today. Per our call, I wanted to capture the two open asks so your team can route to procurement and your channel ops partner: 

1) SKU / packaging confirmation: Globex asked whether the Reserved Capacity SKU set can remain unchanged if we map to an aggregated line item in the PO. We need a short table that shows (a) Redwood SKU code, (b) suggested consolidated PO description, and (c) fiscal treatment (list price vs committed). I attached a working sku_map_redwood_v1.csv — please confirm whether the consolidated descriptions will work for finance.

2) Channel margin evidence for distributor passback: your legal procurement team requested examples of invoices and the reseller routing to validate margin passback. I've attached an example invoice (invoice_sample_Globex_Q3.pdf) and a short explanation below of how passback flows in our marketplace/private-offer model. If procurement wants redlined language for the PO's pass-through section we can provide that.

Action items / next steps:
- Lena: can you confirm who in procurement handles invoice evidence and whether the attached invoice sample suffices?
- Ben: can you produce a one-page margin waterfall (list price -> marketplace fee -> reseller net) we can share by EOD Monday?
- Jordan: can you double-check there are no SKU naming conflicts with earlier partner offers for Globex in EMEA?

Attach: sku_map_redwood_v1.csv, invoice_sample_Globex_Q3.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up with procurement if helpful.

Best,
Soojin

Redwood quick explainer (short): marketplace private-offer passback typically shows the gross list, marketplace commission/transaction fee, any reseller uplift, and then the net payable to the partner. We supply invoice examples plus a reconciliation spreadsheet upon request.

Hi all — attaching the margin waterfall PDF as promised (named margin_waterfall_for_globex.pdf in my notes). Quick summary for procurement:

- Row 1: Unit list price (public/private-offer list).
- Row 2: Marketplace transaction fee (percentage applied at invoice time).
- Row 3: Reseller / distributor passback (fixed percentage applied to net or a per-SKU uplift depending on the agreement).
- Row 4: Net to partner / reseller (what appears on their payout statements).

Clarifying notes: if Globex prefers to show the marketplace fee as an explicit separate line on the invoice we can do that; alternatively we can present a single consolidated gross line and provide a reconciliation file monthly. Both approaches are supported operationally but procurement should confirm the visibility requirement. 

Soojin: added two bullet points for Jordan on historical EMEA naming collisions in the doc comments. Lena: if procurement wants the redlined PO language, tell us whether you accept a short passback clause (we can draft 2 variants: explicit invoice line vs reconciliation attachment).

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: Pricing ops sync: package alignment & channel-margin evidence

Lena — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the PO template. Procurement: to keep things moving, our proposal is the following (pick one):

Option A (preferred if accounting needs invoice-level visibility): include a separate line called "Marketplace fee (Redwood)" on each invoiced line item and a second line called "Reseller passback (partner)" when applicable. We will supply monthly reconciliations.

Option B (preferred if you want minimal PO churn): show a single gross billed line per consolidated SKU and accept a monthly reconciliation attachment that details marketplace commissions and reseller passbacks.

Operational asks from Globex to confirm: 
- Which option does procurement prefer?
- Who at Globex will be the document owner for redline review?
- Any tax or withholdings we should be aware of in your AP process that would affect passback amounts?

If procurement prefers Option A we will draft suggested PO language and a one-page appendix for invoice formatting. Happy to schedule a 30-minute call to finalize.

Jordan
